what: highlight "prevented 1.33 million sales between 2022Q2 and 2023Q4"
said: In March twenty twenty-four, researchers at the Federal Housing Finance Agency published a strange number. One point three three million home sales in America that should have happened, and never did.

what: highlight "nearly all 50 million active mortgages have fixed rates"
said: The FHFA paper says it directly. Nearly all fifty million active mortgages in the United States have fixed rates.

what: highlight "most have interest rates far below prevailing market rates, creating a disincentive to sell"
said: The paper's words: most of these loans have rates far below today's, which creates a disincentive to sell.

what: highlight "the probability of sale is decreased by 18.1%"
said: And they measured it. For every one percentage point that market rates sit above your own rate, your chance of selling falls by eighteen point one percent.

what: highlight "led to a 57% reduction in home sales with fixed-rate mortgages in 2023Q4"
said: By the end of twenty twenty-three, sales of homes with fixed-rate loans were down fifty-seven percent because of this lock-in alone.

what: highlight "results in people not living in homes they would prefer"
said: People call this golden handcuffs. Your cheap rate is so valuable that it keeps you in a house you might not even want anymore.

what: highlight "which decreased prices by 3.3%"
said: The FHFA did the math on both sides. Higher rates on their own pushed prices down by three point three percent.

what: highlight "The supply reduction increased home prices by 5.7%"
said: But the missing supply pushed prices up by five point seven percent. The handcuffs won. So prices went up.

what: highlight "the U.S. housing shortage has declined slightly to 3.7 million units"
said: Freddie Mac, the government-backed mortgage company, estimates the country is short three point seven million homes.

what: highlight "Despite adding 5.8 million housing units over approximately four years"
said: And here's the frustrating part. America did build again. Five point eight million homes in about four years. But demand grew by almost the same amount, so the hole barely shrank.

what: highlight "75% of land zoned for residential uses is zoned single-family"
said: And in many American cities, about seventy-five percent of the land for homes allows only one thing. A single detached house on its own lot. No duplex. No small apartment building.

what: highlight "94% San Jose, California"
said: In San Jose, California, it's ninety-four percent. In Los Angeles, seventy-five. In Portland, Oregon, seventy-seven.

what: highlight "originated in 1916 in the Elmwood neighborhood of Berkeley, California"
said: Where did that come from? Wikipedia traces it to nineteen sixteen, in the Elmwood neighborhood of Berkeley, California.

what: highlight "Single-family zoning both increases the cost of housing units and decreases the supply."
said: The effect is simple. When you can only build one home where four could fit, you get fewer homes, and each one costs more.

what: highlight "opposition by residents to proposed real estate and infrastructure developments in their local area"
said: And when a builder does ask to build more, local residents often show up at city meetings to stop it. There's even a name for that. NIMBY. Not in my back yard.

what: highlight "bought 1,000 distressed houses in Phoenix, Arizona"
said: Between twenty ten and twenty eleven, a company called Treehouse bought one thousand distressed houses in Phoenix, Arizona.

what: highlight "The company was acquired by Blackstone Inc in the spring of 2012"
said: In the spring of twenty twelve, Blackstone, one of the biggest investment firms in the world, bought it and formed Invitation Homes.

what: highlight "the company owned 86,192 rental homes"
said: By December twenty twenty-five, Invitation Homes owned eighty-six thousand one hundred ninety-two rental houses. The largest owner of single-family rentals in the country.

what: highlight "The company's largest markets are Atlanta (12.9% of 2025 revenue)"
said: Its biggest market is Atlanta, which brought in almost thirteen percent of its revenue in twenty twenty-five.

what: highlight "30% were all-cash buyers"
said: The National Association of Realtors found that thirty percent of repeat buyers paid all cash in its twenty twenty-five report.

what: highlight "We're seeing buyers with significant housing equity making larger down payments and all-cash offers, while first-time buyers continue to struggle to enter the market."
said: Their own economist called it a tale of two cities. Owners with equity make big down payments and cash offers, while first-time buyers struggle to get in.

what: highlight "Gifts or loans from family and friends (22%)"
said: And for first-time buyers who do make it, more than one in five used gifts or loans from family and friends for the down payment. The bank of mom and dad.

what: highlight "dropped to a record low of 21%"
said: First-time buyers made up just twenty-one percent of all home purchases. The lowest share ever recorded.

what: highlight "climbed to an all-time high of 40 years"
said: And the typical first-time buyer was forty years old. The oldest ever recorded.

what: highlight "contracted by 50% since 2007"
said: NAR says the share of first-time buyers has shrunk by half since two thousand seven.

what: highlight "Delayed or denied homeownership until age 40 instead of 30 can mean losing roughly $150,000 in equity on a typical starter home."
said: And waiting costs real money. Their estimate: buying at forty instead of thirty can mean losing about one hundred fifty thousand dollars of equity on a typical starter home.

what: highlight "Median time in home before selling: 11 years"
said: Meanwhile, owners are staying put longer than ever. The typical seller had lived in their home for eleven years, another all-time high.

what: highlight "Certain borrower groups with lower wealth accumulation are less able to strategically time their sales, worsening inequality"
said: And the FHFA paper adds one more line. People with less wealth are the least able to time their sales well, which makes inequality worse.

what: highlight "In 2018, Minneapolis became the first major city in the US to end single-family zoning"
said: Some places changed the rules. In twenty eighteen, Minneapolis became the first major American city to end single-family zoning, and allowed duplexes and triplexes in every neighborhood.

what: highlight "SB 1069 and AB 2299 are California bills approved in 2016"
said: California went after backyards. In twenty sixteen it passed laws that limit how much cities can block small backyard homes, called accessory dwelling units.

what: highlight "allow the purchaser of a home to take over the existing terms of the mortgage including; the interest rate"
said: Then there's the loan itself. Some mortgages, like many government-backed ones, are assumable. A buyer can take over the seller's loan, including the old low rate.

what: highlight "Mortgage assumptions have gained popularity since 2022"
said: Those deals have gained popularity since twenty twenty-two, for exactly this reason. But most loans don't allow it.
